title: Split Index · What it does
style:
TEXT MUST BE READABLE. Every single text item on every slide MUST use the LIGHT BLACK BACKGROUND text style, so it stays legible over a photograph of any brightness. Never use a plain text style with no background behind it, and never use white text on its own.

The one permitted alternative is the hook on the first slide, which may use the WHITE BACKGROUND text style instead. It must still have a background.

Keep every text item at 80% width or less so lines never run to the edge of the frame.

I want EXACTLY 4 slides (NO MORE THAN 4 TOTAL SLIDES). Every image is a screenshot of the app itself, so text must never sit over the number or chart it is describing.

Slide 1 is the hook: 1 text item in EXTRA LARGE font size at 90% width, WHITE BACKGROUND text style, sitting on the BOTTOM 1/3RD of the slide. Carry the hook line exactly as given.

Slides 2 and 3 have 2 text items each in SMALL font size at 80% width, LIGHT BLACK BACKGROUND text style, on the TOP 1/3RD. The first names one capability from the permitted list below, the second says what it gives someone who both lifts and runs.

Slide 4 has 2 text items, LIGHT BLACK BACKGROUND, on the TOP 1/3RD: the first reads 'Split Index' in EXTRA LARGE font size, the second reads exactly 'free to download - link in bio' in SMALL font size. No other text and no numbers on slide 4.

Use the default TikTok font throughout.

Written in a blunt, data-led tone with short declarative sentences, first person where it reads naturally. Use contractions the way a person speaks: don't, didn't, that's, you're. No hype, no emojis, no exclamation marks. 6 to 12 words per text item.

The subject is always hybrid training: how lifting and running affect each other, and how one athlete can be measured across both. Never compare two lifts against each other as if that were the point — the comparison that matters is strength against endurance.

ONLY these things may be named as something the app does. This list is exhaustive:
  - the Split Index, one score out of 100 combining strength and endurance
  - the Engine score for endurance and the Lab score for strength
  - predicted race times at 1500m, 5k, 10k, half and marathon, from the athlete's own pace curve
  - a personal fatigue exponent regressed from their own maximal efforts, instead of a population average
  - adaptive 1RM per lift: what recent training says they could lift today, against their all-time best, with a likely range
  - DOTS and IPF GL, bodyweight-adjusted strength scores
  - the interference measurement: how their lifting affects their running and the reverse, from their own paired sessions
  - injury risk as this week's load against their rolling four-week average
  - a readiness score for today
  - efficiency factor, meaning speed per heartbeat
  - an estimated lactate threshold and an estimated VO2max, both clearly estimates
  - a Hybrid Plan whose sessions each state the reason they were prescribed
  - per-set scoring in the gym, where each set is scored on its own

Do not name any metric, score or feature outside that list. Do not invent a plausible-sounding name for one. If you cannot make the point using something on the list, make a different point.

NEVER state what is typical, normal, balanced, average or good for most people. The app scores an athlete against their own history and against published standards; it does not hold a norm for every ratio, so any sentence of that shape is an invention.

EVERY number you write must either appear word-for-word in the hook line, or be arithmetic on two numbers that do — a ratio or a percentage of them. You may NOT write any other weight, time, date, duration, percentage or count. Not one. If a sentence needs a number you do not have, write the sentence without a number. Inventing a plausible figure is the single worst thing you can do here.

Never make a medical claim. Injury risk is always relative to the athlete's own baseline, never a diagnosis. Never describe age or sex adjustments as accurate or calibrated, because they are beta.
slideshow_hooks: One score for lifting and running. Not two apps arguing.
It predicts five race times from runs you actually did.
Every lift you do, scored on its own curve. Not just the big three.
Strength 81.7. Endurance 70.1. One athlete, scored honestly.
It measures what your lifting costs your running. From your sessions, not a study.

caption.prompt_text: Write a TikTok caption under 150 characters for Split Index, a hybrid-fitness app that scores lifting and running on one scale out of 100 from the user's own logged sessions. End with: Search Split Index on the App Store. Blunt and specific, no emojis, at most one hashtag. Never make medical claims; frame injury risk as relative to the athlete's own baseline.

description.prompt_text: One or two plain sentences expanding the hook for a hybrid athlete. State what the app measures across strength and endurance and why the number is defensible. No hype, no medical claims. Never state age or sex factors as calibrated accuracy. Then end with 4 to 6 hashtags on their own line, drawn from this pool and matched to the post: #hybridathlete #hybridtraining #hyrox #runningtips #powerlifting #strengthandconditioning #marathontraining #gymtok #runtok #fitnessapp
